passage:
Wednesday: In assembly, Neelam's voice cracked in the middle of the pledge, up to a squeak and back down. A few boys sniggered. Neelam's face burned and he stared at his shoes. Gargi, standing next to him, kept looking straight ahead as if nothing had happened.
Thursday: Neelam whispered in class and hid the cracks. At lunch, Gargi said, "Your voice is changing, that's normal. Nobody minds."
Saturday: His father said, "Mine did that. It settles." Neelam read aloud at home, cracks and all, and they laughed together.

qa.q: On which day did Neelam's voice crack in assembly?
What was Neelam feeling when he stared at his shoes?
qa.a: He was embarrassed, and his face burned after the boys sniggered. The crack was physical, not emotional.
Gargi ignored the crack in assembly and later said it was normal and nobody minded. Kind peers ignore it.

qa.q: How might Neelam's father seeing it help him?
qa.a: His father said his own voice did that and it settles, which offered reassurance. Neelam could read aloud and laugh.

grounding: A teenager's voice cracks in puberty causing embarrassment, and kind peers and adults reassure that it settles.

passage: Thomas, your grandfather has a story. I'm Noor, and at fourteen I was called to read the morning prayers at the school assembly. Halfway through, my voice cracked. It went up like a whistle, then down like a frog. Boys giggled. My ears burned. But the master, who I'd been afraid of, didn't smile. He said gently after, "Voices do that at your age. It settles in time." A boy called Anwar said, "I didn't even notice," though I knew he did. It settled after a few months. Your voice will do it too, and when it does, let it. Laugh if you like.

qa.q: How old was Noor when he was asked to read the morning prayers?
What was Noor feeling when his voice cracked in assembly?
qa.a: He was embarrassed, since his ears burned and boys giggled. The crack was just physical.

qa.q: What advice does Noor give Thomas?
qa.a: When his voice cracks, let it and laugh if he likes, since it settles in time. Adults and friends can reassure him.

qa.q: How might Anwar's remark have felt for Noor?
qa.a: Noor knew Anwar probably noticed but appreciated that he chose to ignore it. Kindness spared him.

grounding: A teenager's voice cracks in puberty, and an elder tells Thomas that kind peers ignore it and it settles.
